subject: ventures/qcd-calculator
professional: a CPA/EA who prepares returns for retirees; first checks: the 2026 constants (QCD limit, standard and 65+ amounts, brackets, OBBBA senior deduction and charitable rules), the provisional-income worksheet for taxable Social Security, how the QCD is reported (1040 line 4a/4b), and that every filing status offered gets its own figures

evidence.correctness: Constants checked against published 2026 figures from my own knowledge of Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (post-OBBBA) and the IRS 2026 QCD indexation (irs.gov not fetched): standard 16,100/32,200, extra 65+ 2,050 single / 1,650 married, single and MFJ bracket tops, QCD limit 111,000, senior deduction 6,000 with 6% phase-out over 75k/150k MAGI (OBBBA, 2025-2028), 0.5%-of-AGI floor on itemized gifts and 1,000/2,000 non-itemizer cash deduction from 2026, SS base amounts 25k/34k and 32k/44k (IRC 86) all match. Hand recomputation from the Pub 915 worksheet and the bracket table of four cases (`node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/f59c5cce-fbdc-5341-97d2-6a5629e767ca/scratchpad/qcd/run.mjs`, plus a low-income one-liner): defaults single none/cash/QCD tax 10,679.60/10,459.60/8,347.60, advantage 2,612 (incl. 500 state); MFJ 2x65 tax 19,553/19,113/16,055, senior 10,050 vs 10,950; itemizer cash deduction 49,522.50 = 40,000+10,000-0.005x95,500; low-income case taxable SS 7,050 -> 2,000 under QCD (50% tier) and tax 790 -> 0. All match to the cent. Not a 3: the filing-status choice is labelled 'Single or head of household' but HoH uses single figures; with HoH's 24,150 standard deduction and HoH brackets (`node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/f59c5cce-fbdc-5341-97d2-6a5629e767ca/scratchpad/qcd/hoh.mjs`) the default case's federal tax is 7,390 not 10,680 and the QCD advantage 1,652 not 2,612 (58% overstated). Also a user under 70 1/2 still gets 'A QCD saves $2,112' under the warning.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features run end to end in calc.mjs: QCD vs cash vs no gift, AGI, taxable SS, senior deduction, federal and flat state tax, after-tax cost, RMD left, gift-size grid (0.5x/1x/2x), return lines table and CSV export, opt-out usage counter. The 'head of household' option the select offers is not actually modelled. No stubs or TODOs; related-tool links point at sibling ventures; served copy has the marisstella.app origin (`node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs qcd-calculator`: no placeholder origins).
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/qcd-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 25 tests, 25 pass, 86 ms. Five seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: senior phase rate 0.06->0.05, the SS second-tier min 0.5(b2-b1) +1000, single 22% bracket rate -> 24%, single extra-65 2,050->2,000 all SURVIVED; charity floor 0.005->0.01 caught. Tests assert relations (QCD <= cash, AGI lower) and one bracket boundary, but no full worked return with a hand-checked total, so almost every constant and the senior phase-out are unpinned.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (131 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script. Pure functions, figures in one injectable FIGURES block, no dependencies, output escaped, storage access guarded. Defects: blank or unparsable fields silently become the example values (index.html:137, so a cleared IRA field computes on 40,000), making analyze's 'must be a number' warning unreachable from the page; the age < 70 1/2 check only warns and the QCD verdict is still printed (calc.mjs:101, index.html:149); age and numOver65 are not cross-checked.
evidence.claims: Backed: 2026 figures (checked above), IRC 408(d)(8) basics, RMD first-dollars and DAF/supporting-org exclusions in the FAQ, the 'Not decided' list (IRMAA, NIIT, AMT, per-spouse limit), disclaimer on page, README and llms.txt, privacy line matches usage.mjs (local storage, DNT/GPC honoured). Not backed: the select label 'Single or head of household' (index.html:90) while only single figures exist; the return-lines label 'QCD excluded (1099-R box 2a lower by)' (calc.mjs:116): custodians do not reduce box 2a for a QCD; Pub 590-B and the 1040 instructions have the full amount on line 4a, the taxable part on 4b and 'QCD' written next to it (from 2025 the 1099-R may carry code Y); the code comment and README say ordinary-only rates do not affect the QCD-vs-cash difference (calc.mjs:10-11), but with qualified dividends a QCD shifts how much falls in the 0%/15% bands, so it can.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a preparer with a single or MFJ retiree enters IRA distribution, SS, pension, other itemized and gift and gets a correct side-by-side with the SS and senior-deduction knock-ons and a CSV, enough for a year-end QCD conversation. Hit in the first hour: an HoH or widowed client gets wrong figures under a label that says it handles them; no MFS; a couple gets one shared QCD limit; the post-70 1/2 deductible-IRA-contribution offset (408(d)(8)(A) as amended by SECURE 2019) and the one-time split-interest QCD (SECURE 2.0) are not modelled or mentioned; clients with qualified dividends get ordinary-rate tax; state tax is a flat rate on AGI including taxable SS, which most states exempt.
evidence.domain: Method matches practice for the core: exclusion from AGI, Pub 915 provisional-income tiers, OBBBA senior deduction phase-out on MAGI, the 0.5% floor applied to itemizers only, the non-itemizer deduction stacked on the standard deduction, excess over the cap treated as cash. Departures: HoH treated as single; the 1099-R box 2a reporting statement is wrong; anti-abuse offset absent and undisclosed; 60%-of-AGI cash limit not applied; preferential-rate stacking ignored with a claim that it does not matter.

defects.what: The filing-status select offers 'Single or head of household' but FIGURES has only single and MFJ, so an HoH filer is computed with the single 16,100 standard deduction and single brackets: on the default inputs federal tax 10,680 instead of 7,390 and the QCD advantage 2,612 instead of 1,652.

Return-lines table labels the QCD 'QCD excluded (1099-R box 2a lower by)'; custodians do not reduce box 2a for a QCD. Pub 590-B / 1040 instructions: full distribution on line 4a, taxable part on 4b, 'QCD' next to 4b.
Under age 70 1/2 the tool warns but still computes and headlines 'A QCD saves $X' as if the QCD were available.
Blank or unparsable inputs silently fall back to the example values (a cleared IRA distribution computes on 40,000), so analyze's 'must be a number' warning never reaches the page.

Four of five seeded mutants in core constants and formulas (senior phase-out rate, SS second-tier term, a bracket rate, extra-65 amount) leave all 25 tests green; no test pins a full worked return against hand-computed totals.
The post-70 1/2 deductible IRA contribution offset (408(d)(8)(A), SECURE Act 2019) and the one-time split-interest QCD (SECURE 2.0) are neither modelled nor listed under 'Not modelled'.

Comment and model note claim ordinary-only rates overstate tax 'but not the QCD-versus-cash difference'; with qualified dividends a QCD changes how much falls in the 0%/15% bands, so the difference can change.
State tax is a flat rate on AGI including taxable Social Security, which most income-tax states exempt, overstating the state side of the QCD saving when taxable SS moves.

verdict: For a single or married-joint retiree with ordinary income the arithmetic is right: four worked cases recomputed by hand from the Pub 915 worksheet, the 2026 brackets and standard deductions, and the OBBBA senior deduction and 0.5% floor match to the cent, and every 2026 constant checks out. Three things keep it below the bar. The select says 'Single or head of household' but HoH runs on single figures, overstating an HoH filer's tax by about 3,300 dollars and the QCD saving by 58% on the default inputs. The return-lines table tells a preparer that 1099-R box 2a is lowered by the QCD, which is not how a QCD is reported. And the tests pin almost nothing: four of five seeded mutants in core constants survive. Smaller gaps: under-70 1/2 users still see a QCD saving, blank fields silently become example values, and the anti-abuse offset and split-interest QCD go unmentioned.
